what: Which low RAM a call attempt touches, compared with AT&T8
board: 20.16 MHz Courier V.Everything, ID_SDL v4.03d, supervisor 7.4.16, DSP 3.1.2
method: 0x5A markers written to 27 addresses across 0x1600-0xf000, NOTHING armed, ATDT9099 dialled, the attempt run to completion, ATH0, then the markers read back.

the call.outcome: no result code for 60 s, then NO CARRIER - the S7 carrier timeout
the call.interpretation: The modem went off hook and dialled; nothing answered with a carrier. A second attempt with ATX4 (dial tone and busy detection enabled) also produced no NO DIALTONE inside 25 s, which is what a present line looks like - a missing line reports NO DIALTONE quickly under X4.
the call.important: This is a sweep across a call ATTEMPT, not a connected data call. No carrier was ever established, so the datapump never ran a handshake.

result.cleared: none - not one marker was zeroed

conclusion: A call does not clear 0x3000-0x8000. That erasure is specific to the &T8 self-test, not to normal operation, so the sampler's old 0x3000 placement was not necessarily unsafe for a call - it was unsafe for the test being used to validate it. The current placement at 0x1a00 with the ring ending at 0x2b00 survives both, and 0x2c00 is written in both cases, which is why the ring stops short of it.
still untested: A connected call. The three addresses a call attempt writes are all outside the sampler's region, but a real handshake exercises the datapump and may touch more. The sweep should be repeated against a number that answers before a capture is trusted.
